title: Kongnamul Muchim Seasoned Soybean Sprouts
shortDescription: Soybean sprouts are cooked until tender but crisp, drained, and seasoned with garlic, scallion, toasted sesame oil, sesame seeds, and a restrained touch of gochugaru.
culturalContext: Kongnamul muchim is an everyday Korean soybean-sprout banchan with mild and spicy variations. Some cooks simmer with little water while others blanch; this draft uses a covered simmer and requires testing for the exact sprout size and stove output.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.preparation: discolored sprouts and loose hulls removed

instructions.heading: Sort and rinse
instructions.action: Discard slimy, dark, or damaged sprouts. Rinse the remaining sprouts thoroughly under cool running water and drain.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Sprouts look firm and pale with crisp yellow heads and no off odor.
instructions.safetyNote: Sprouts can carry pathogens; keep them refrigerated and do not taste them raw.

instructions.heading: Set the covered simmer
instructions.action: Put sprouts, water, and half the salt in a saucepan. Cover tightly and bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Steam escapes around the lid and the liquid boils steadily.
instructions.safetyNote: Once heating begins, keep the lid closed for the timed cook to maintain consistent heat.

instructions.heading: Cook through
instructions.action: Reduce to medium and cook covered for 5 minutes. Remove from heat, uncover away from your face, and check that the sprouts are hot and tender-crisp with no raw-bean aroma.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Stems bend easily but retain a slight snap, and the raw grassy aroma is gone.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not shorten the cooking step or serve raw sprouts in this recipe.

instructions.heading: Drain and cool
instructions.action: Drain immediately in a clean colander and spread in a clean bowl for 10 minutes; do not rinse after cooking.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Steam subsides and no water pools in the bowl.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean equipment so cooked sprouts do not contact the raw-sprout sink area.

instructions.heading: Season
instructions.action: Add garlic, scallions, sesame oil, sesame seeds, optional gochugaru, and remaining salt. Toss gently until evenly coated.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Sprouts are glossy and evenly flecked with scallion and sesame.

instructions.heading: Serve or refrigerate
instructions.action: Serve warm or cool, or transfer promptly to a shallow covered container and refrigerate.
instructions.safetyNote: Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep at or below 40°F / 4°C.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan is simmered on the stovetop.
visualDonenessCues: Stems bend easily while retaining a slight snap
foodSafetyNotes: Buy refrigerated sprouts and reject slimy, darkened, or sour-smelling packages.
Keep sprouts refrigerated and do not taste them raw.
Cook covered until hot throughout and the raw-bean aroma is gone.
Separate cooked sprouts from raw-sprout tools and sink splash.
Refrigerate within 2 hours at or below 40°F / 4°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy and sesame; verify packaged gochugaru and sesame labels for facility cross-contact.

substitutions: Mung bean sprouts are not a direct substitute for this named dish and need a separate cooking-time test.
Omit gochugaru for a mild version.
ingredientSourcing: Choose refrigerated soybean sprouts with firm white stems, bright yellow heads, and no excess liquid.
Use freshly toasted sesame seeds for a clear nutty aroma.
makeAhead: This dish is best cooked and seasoned the day it is served; aromatics may be prepared several hours ahead under refrigeration.
storage: Refrigerate in a shallow airtight container within 2 hours and use within 3 days; this conservative limit requires food-safety approval.
reheating: Serve cold, cool, or briefly warm in a covered skillet; do not repeatedly reheat and cool.
leftovers: Add properly refrigerated leftovers to a hot rice bowl just before serving within the approved storage window.
servingSuggestions: Serve in small portions with rice
Offer mild and gochugaru-seasoned versions as separate batches

faq.question: Why keep the lid on while cooking?
faq.answer: A covered cook provides steady steam and heat so the sprouts cook evenly and lose their raw grassy aroma.

faq.question: Can I serve soybean sprouts raw?
faq.answer: Not in this recipe; the sprouts are intentionally cooked through before seasoning.
